title: The SSF conformance PR added GET/PATCH/PUT stream handlers plus stream verify and status views without the add_stream provider permission check that the existing POST handler enforces, so any token holder for the app can read, modify, verify and disable its event streams.

findings.explanation: The diff does not introduce any raw SQL queries or string concatenation into SQL statements. The changes involve Django ORM filters (e.g., `self.backchannel_providers.filter`) and standard Django model operations, which are safe against SQL injection by default.

The `SSFStreamViewSet` is modified to include `DestroyModelMixin`, enabling the DELETE endpoint. However, the viewset inherits from `GenericViewSet` and uses `queryset = Stream.objects.all()`. In the authentik framework (and Django REST Framework generally), authorization is enforced via `get_permissions` or `get_queryset` overrides in the base classes or mixins (like `EnterpriseRequiredMixin` seen in the serializer). The `Stream` model is tied to a `provider` which is tied to an `application`. The standard authentik API patterns ensure that only users with the appropriate permissions (e.g., `authentik_providers_ssf.stream_delete`) can access these endpoints. The diff does not show any bypass of these checks or direct access to objects without permission verification. The addition of `DestroyModelMixin` is a standard way to enable deletion, and the security relies on the existing permission framework which is not modified to be insecure in this diff.
